deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 121, 'Topologie modérée', 1974). On the preceding pages Grothendieck sets up a family F of subsets of a set or space X. F is generated by a family F_0 of 'closed' pieces and is subject to conditions a)–f): Boolean-type stability, closure stability, local closedness, and finiteness of connected components (f). To F he attaches the algebra A_(F) of Λ-valued functions that are 'constructible' with respect to F. This page opens §2, the basic finite example: finite partitions.

(1) Let P = (X_i)_{i∈I} be a finite partition of X. Let F_P be the set of all unions of the X_i, a finite Boolean algebra. Then F_P satisfies the Boolean conditions (b, and a which is struck or ambiguous). A_(F_P) is the algebra of functions X→Λ that are constant on each X_i, i.e. functions factoring through the quotient set X/R, where R is the equivalence relation of the partition.

(2) Now let X be a topological space. Condition c) (stability of F under closure) is equivalent to:
1°) each closure cl(X_i) is a union of strata, i.e. is R-saturated. This is the classical 'frontier condition' of stratification theory.

(3) A struck-out attempt tried to show that 1° alone forces local closedness. Grothendieck abandons it and introduces a second condition:
2°) cl(X_i) = cl(X_j) implies i = j.
A struck-out argument (and the bottom-left margin) shows the converse direction: 1° plus local closedness implies 2°. If cl X_i = cl X_j with X_i open in its closure, then the dense subset X_j meets X_i, so i = j.

(4) Claim: 1° and 2° together imply that every X_i is locally closed. The proof is on the next page.
- Order I by i ≼ j iff cl X_i ⊂ cl X_j. This is a preorder, and by 2° a partial order (the 'incidence relation of the leaves').
- Take a minimal stratum X_{i0}. Its closure is a union of strata X_j with cl X_j ⊂ cl X_{i0}. By minimality and 2°, the only such stratum is X_{i0}, so X_{i0} is closed.
- Remove it, pass to the open set X − X_{i0} with the induced partition, and induct on the number of strata.

The next page then calls a finite partition satisfying 1° and 2° a 'stratification admissible' ('strict' if the strata are connected). It notes that F_P is then generated by a family of closed sets F_0, so condition d) holds automatically.

Modern reading: given 1°, condition 2° says precisely that the finite quotient space X/R is T0. So an admissible stratification is the same as a quotient map X → (finite poset with Alexandrov topology) such that the closure of each fibre is the preimage of the closure of the point. The function algebra A_(F_P) is then the algebra of Λ-valued functions pulled back from this finite poset. The purpose is to supply the simplest model for the axiomatics of tame ('modérée') subsets and their function algebras.
errors: No error in the final argument. The induction needs (and Grothendieck checks or uses) that 1° and 2° pass to the open subspace X − X_{i0}. This holds because closures in an open U containing X_i equal cl(X_i) ∩ U, and cl(X_i) is recovered as the closure of cl_U(X_i). Grothendieck does not spell this out.

The first struck-out attempt (that 1° alone gives local closedness, via 'cl X_j ∩ X_i = ∅ when X_j ⊂ cl X_i') was rightly abandoned; 1° alone does not suffice. Example: X a two-point indiscrete space partitioned into two points; 1° holds, the points are not locally closed, and 2° fails.
Finiteness of I is essential for the minimal-element induction. Grothendieck added 'finie' as an insertion, which is correct.

ideas.what: Finite partition gives a Boolean algebra F_P; its constructible-function algebra is the functions factoring through X/R
ideas.modern_name: Constructible functions relative to a finite partition / functions on a finite quotient
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced only programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Closure-stability of F_P is equivalent to the closure of each stratum being a union of strata
Frontier condition plus distinct closures for distinct strata is equivalent to frontier condition plus locally closed strata; proved by induction on minimal strata of the incidence order
ideas.modern_name: Strata poset; stratification as a map to a finite T0 (Alexandrov) space
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; poset-stratified spaces formalized by Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s)

ideas.what: Incidence order on strata ('relation d'incidence des feuilles'), with minimal strata closed
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata / specialization order on X/R

missed.claim: The notes implicitly identify 'admissible finite stratifications' with partitions whose quotient X/R is a finite T0 space (a poset) compatible with closures. This is the modern 'poset-stratified space' viewpoint, written in 1974 as the base case of an axiomatics of tame topology with function algebras A_(F). The left margin note about 'le problème ... X/R ... F_P' suggests he was considering the quotient as the organizing object.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it is an early instance (1974) of treating stratifications as maps to finite posets inside a tame-topology axiomatics, anticipating Lurie and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. Mathematically it is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains careful but elementary point-set lemmas on finite stratifications: the frontier condition, the T0 condition on the quotient, and local closedness of strata. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of the unpublished 1974 tame-topology axiomatics that pre-dates Esquisse; no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Section title likely '§ 2) (Décompositions admissibles)' or similar; the next page uses 'stratification admissible'. Uncertain.

The left-margin note 'Mais 1° + les X_i loc. fermés implique ...' is in the bottom-left margin, not the top. It most likely reads 'implique 2°', i.e. the converse direction of the struck-out argument.
In 'Comme c) est vérifié trivialement' the circled symbol is ambiguous and may be another condition label (e.g. ② or d)); the whole passage is struck out.
The insertion over 'partition' reads 'finie', correctly placed: 'une partition finie de X'.
'satisfait les conditions a), b)': 'a)' appears scribbled or overwritten in the image.
